entry.name: mc.voiceallocator~
entry.description: The mc.voiceallocator~ object assigns voice numbers to incoming messages using an optional multichannel signal to determine voice busy state. It also maintains a voice busy map used by other MC objects to avoid unnecessary processing for channels that are not actively producing audio in response to events.

arguments.name: voice count
arguments.description: An optional argument can set a maximum number of voice numbers theobject will use. If no argument is supplied, the default voice count is 0, meaning thatwill set its maximum voice count by the number of channels in a connected multichannel input. If there is no connected multichannel input, the default voice count is 16.

attributes.name: initialbusystate
attributes.digest: Initial Busy State
attributes.description: Sets the initial busy state. The default value is 1. Set this to zero to avoid high CPU usage before sending events when audio is turned on.

attributes.name: steal
attributes.digest: Voice Stealing
attributes.description: When set to 1, theattribute allows messages to pass through mc.voiceallocator~ and are assigned to voice numbers when all voices have been allocated. When set to 0, messages are not passed through and are not assigned to voice numbers if all voices are already allocated.

attributes.name: voices
attributes.digest: Voice Count
attributes.description: Theattribute sets the maximum voice numberwill allocate and output. Whenis 0 (the default), the active voice count is determined by the number of channels in the connected multichannel signal. If there is no connected signal,defaults to 16 voices.

messages.name: anything
messages.description: The message is repeated to the left outlet preceded by a new voice number sent out the right outlet.

messages.name: bang
messages.description: Themessage is repeated to the left outlet preceded by a new voice number sent out the right outlet.

messages.name: endevent
messages.description: The word, followed by an event name defined by themessage, releases the voice associated with the event. The entiremessage is repeated to the left outlet.

messages.name: event
messages.description: The word, followed by an event name and a message, sends the entiremessage out the left outlet preceded by a newly allocated voice number. The name can later be used with themessage to release the voice that became associated with the event.

messages.name: float
messages.description: The number is repeated to the left outlet preceded by a new voice number sent out the right outlet.

messages.name: holdevent
messages.digest: Starts and holds a named event
messages.description: The word, followed by an event name and a message, sends the entiremessage out the left outlet preceded by a newly allocated voice number. The name can later be used with themessage to release the voice that became associated with the event. Unlike themessage,explicitly holds the named event until connected audio reaches zero.

messages.name: int
messages.description: The number is repeated to the left outlet preceded by a new voice number sent out the right outlet.

messages.name: list
messages.description: The list is repeated to the left outlet preceded by a new voice number sent out the right outlet.

messages.name: printbusymap
messages.description: Prints the current state of thebusy map to the Max Console as a list.

messages.name: release
messages.description: The word, followed by a voice number, releases that voice number (sets to a non-busy state). Without an argument,sets all voices to a non-busy state.

messages.name: releaseevent
messages.description: The word, followed by an event name defined by anmessage, releases the voice number associated with the named event but unlike, does not produce a message out the left outlet.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: Connect an optional multichannel signal to preventfrom reallocating a voice until the corresponding channel's signal level goes to zero.

inlets.digest: Multichannel signal representing busy state; any message along with specific messages to manage allocating and releasing voices.
inlets.description: A multichannel signal connected to's left inlet establishes a voice busy state. Typically you'll connect the multichannel output of audio triggered by events passing through. This permits you to hold a voice busy after an event that release a voice has been received.Use,, andmessages to manage voice allocation.

outlets.description: Incoming messages are sent out the left outlet, preceded by an associated voice number out the right outlet.
An allocated voice number is sent immediately prior to its associated message is sent out the left outlet.
